author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: First Saudi state and Wahhabism
summary: In 1744 the reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab settled in Diriyah in Najd, and its prince Muhammad ibn Saud agreed to support his call to purge Islam of distortions. Their lasting alliance founded the First Saudi State, ruled from the citadel of at-Turaif, and from Diriyah the reform message spread through Arabia and the wider Muslim world. The state came to control most of Arabia until the Ottoman sultan had Muhammad Ali send his son Ibrahim Pasha, who routed the Saudi forces in 1817.

uncertainty.note: MWNF gives 1744, a rout of Saudi forces in 1817 and a span of about 75 years; 1818 kept as the end.

as_recorded.value: The First Saudi State was established in 1744
the First Saudi State lasted for about 75 years

where.modern_name: At-Turaif District, Ad Diriyah, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia

importance.justification: Joined the Saud dynasty to Wahhabi reform, the basis of the later Saudi state and a lasting current in Sunni Islam (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: The territorial expansion of the First Saudi State and its capture of the holy sanctuaries in Mecca and Medina challenged Ottoman imperial authority, provoking the Ottoman-Saudi War of 1811–1818.
